The tapetum is part of the anther, and t.why: Common-sense case: people say that a layer is part of the anther and that the anther is part of the stamen; nobody states the chained conclusion on its own.

sources.quote: The tapetum is a specialised  layer of nutritive cells found within the anther of flowering plants, located between the sporogenous tissue and the anther wall.
A stamen typically consists of a stalk called the filament and an anther which contains microsporangia.

sources.query: the anther is part of the stamen
tapetum is part of the stamen
sources.note: The conclusion is not written as a sentence.

The crista ampullaris is part of the sem.why: Common-sense case: each link is the kind of thing anatomy texts say; the chained conclusion is almost never written as a sentence.

sources.quote: They are found in the ampullae of each of the semicircular canals of the inner ear, meaning that there are three pairs in total.
The semicircular canals are three semicircular interconnected tubes located in the innermost part of each ear, the inner ear.

sources.query: crista ampullaris is part of the inner ear
sources.note: The conclusion is rarely written as a sentence.

Insulin is produced by the pancreas..why: Stated explicitly and very often: thousands of exact sentences in Dolma in several wordings, and the lead of Wikipedia's Insulin and Pancreas articles. It follows from nothing a model holds more firmly, so a model holds it directly.

sources.query: insulin is produced by the pancreas
insulin is produced in the pancreas
insulin is produced by the thyroid

sources.quote: a peptide hormone produced by beta cells of the pancreatic islets
Whales are a widely distributed and diverse group of fully aquatic placental marine mammals.

notes: RBox contraction paired with biology-replace-0009: removes the property ('is part of' is transitive), so every query expects 'does not know'. The propositional questions follow strong Kleene logic. The two derived instances give their premises in the prompt and ask about the conclusion; hops counts those premises as one bridge. Unrelated near asks the same kind of property of another relation, which stays as it was (contraction is exempt from Rule 7); unrelated far asks about an unrelated relation.
